_meta.voice: Outcome-first, plain English, grade-7 reading level. Reader is the hero, Fatiha is the guide. No mood taglines, no self-quotes, max one 'not X, but Y' per page, every claim followed by a number or named example.
_meta.identity: Fatiha Chikh · Tech & AI Marketing Expert · 20 years at Dell, Intel, Microsoft
_meta.positioning: Every promise must describe an outcome a 10-year-old could draw. The reader is the hero. Outcome first, operation second. Do not reduce the value to drafting emails or saving a few minutes. The value is helping ambitious professionals build real business capability with AI, step by step. Use proof, named examples and visible before/after outcomes. Avoid jargon in promises. Put technical terms in the explanation, not the headline.

faq.q: I'm not technical. Can I still do this?
faq.a: Yes. You need to understand the work you want done, not learn to code. I explain the tools in plain language and start with the work itself.

faq.q: Do I need an AI agent?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Some work needs a good prompt. Some needs an automation between tools. An agent makes sense when AI needs to complete several steps and return a finished result.

faq.q: What is the difference between the guides and the workbooks?
faq.a: The guides help you use AI in your work and business. The workbooks help you find the patterns in your own experience and decide what to do with them.

faq.q: What if the free guides are not enough?
faq.a: If you want to build something specific, see Build with me. If you want to help a team use AI in real work, explore the workshops.

what_you_get.body: Your logins, your accounts, your tools. When we finish, you own it. No retainer, no keys held back.

workshops.h1: AI your team will actually adopt.
workshops.sub: I led Technology waves, cloud and SaaS adoption across Fortune 500 teams in a dozen markets and five languages. I bring that same playbook in-house: practical, non-technical, built from a business that runs on it.
workshops.cta: Apply to bring this to your team
workshops.why_h2: Adoption is the hard part. That's what I teach.
workshops.why_body: Most AI talks inspire the room and change nothing on Monday. For 20 years my job in big corporations was getting real teams to use new tech, repeatedly, across cultures and time zones. The workshops install a clear method without anyone becoming technical. Your team leaves with a system, not just a slide deck
workshops.formats_h2: Two ways to bring this in.

formats.title: Half-day workshop
formats.body: 3.5 hours. Up to 20 participants. We audit one business area — marketing, operations, or content — and map the exact automation that will move the needle. Your team leaves with a built roadmap, a selected tool stack, and one scoped workflow ready to implement. WIth a plan that fits your business.

formats.title: Full-day workshop
formats.body: 7 hours. Up to 15 participants. We pick one workflow and build it together in the room — live. By the end of the day, your team has a working automation running in their actual tools. Guaranteed. This is not a demo. This is a build. Lunch, templates, and 30 days of follow-up support included.

workshops.guarantee_h2: Your team leaves with one automation built.
workshops.guarantee_body: The full-day workshop comes with a simple guarantee: if we do not have at least one working automation running in your team's tools by the end of the day, I follow up until you do. I have done it for my own business. The method works. The only requirement is that your team shows up ready to build, not just watch.
not_for: You want a motivational keynote. I build systems, not inspiration.
Your team is not ready to touch the tools. This is hands-on, not theory.
You are looking for a technical coding workshop. I work with no-code and low-code tools your team can actually use.
The decision-maker is not in the room. Adoption dies when leadership is not present.
workshops.dynamic_note: Topics change with the news. Each session is based on the latest most valuable information, not the noise or hype so your team works on what matters now but don't get distracted.
